svg.title: RedTeam Copilot scan pipeline and control points
svg.desc: An operator submits a target and module toggles from the browser to an unauthenticated FastAPI endpoint that applies a string-prefix check, then a single background task runs OSINT, port scanning, CVE matching and report generation in fixed order, each summarised by a Groq model; the port scan probes whatever address the target resolves to, results and a PDF go to Supabase, and the ledger lists the three implemented controls and three limits including template-generated evidence in the PDF.
svg.text: WHAT EACH STAGE REACHES OUT TO
Groq · llama-3.3-70b-versatile — called by every stage for analysis text; on failure the error string is returned as text
The only server-side check reads the target string; nmap then
scans whatever address that name resolves to.
Browser: the permission checkbox and domain regex only enable the button.
Neither is sent to, or checked by, the API.
and requires a dot. No auth, allow-list, approval step or rate limit.
Execution: none. A domain that resolves to a private address
passes C2 and is scanned. No automated tests cover any control.
PDF finding cards include “Evidence” request/response text built from
CVEs are NVD keyword matches on nmap’s product string, not confirmed
vulnerabilities. TCP-fallback services have no product and are skipped.
No engagements, agent orchestration or human-approval workflow exist.
SHODAN_API_KEY is listed in .env.example but never read.
